hooks.text: The Milky Way is breathing two massive bubbles of radiation.
Two gargantuan radiation bubbles span half of our entire galaxy.
Our galaxy looks quiet, but it is actually breathing fire.

title: The Milky Way is Hiding Huge Radiation Bubbles
description: NASA discovered two gargantuan bubbles of radiation hiding in the Milky Way. These Fermi bubbles span half the galaxy's diameter and suggest a violent past.

beats.text: The Milky Way is breathing two massive bubbles of radiation.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of the Fermi bubbles extending from the Milky Way core, 2010
queries: Fermi bubbles Milky Way NASA illustration

beats.text: These invisible lobes tower 25,000 light-years above and below us.
beats.visual: Edge-on view diagram of the Milky Way showing symmetric radiation lobes
queries: Milky Way edge-on diagram Fermi bubbles

beats.text: They span half the diameter of our entire galaxy.
beats.visual: Illustration of the full Milky Way disk with bubbles spanning the center

beats.text: A thick fog of background radiation hid them for decades.
beats.visual: NASA Fermi LAT all-sky map showing diffuse gamma-ray background
queries: Fermi LAT all-sky map gamma rays

beats.text: Astronomers finally spotted them using public NASA data in 2010.
beats.visual: Illustration of the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope in Earth orbit
queries: Fermi Gamma-Ray Space Telescope NASA illustration

beats.text: These gargantuan clouds are plasma glowing with high-energy light.
beats.visual: Close-up schematic of energetic plasma lobes at the galactic center

beats.text: We thought our home was a quiet, stable spiral.
beats.visual: Standard spiral galaxy illustration of the Milky Way without bubbles

beats.text: But our galaxy is actually breathing fire into the void.
beats.visual: Dramatic concept of the Milky Way core glowing with violent radiation

beats.text: It's breathing two massive bubbles of radiation.

queries: Fermi bubbles Milky Way NASA illustration

better_than_last: I moved the predictable black hole jet theory to a broader 'fire-breathing' metaphor and emphasized the discovery in public data as a more surprising twist.
